newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 4.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 4. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The badly-fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) has yet to reach a decision on whether it would withdraw from parliament because it has so far secured only 10 seats in the House of Representatives, less than the minimum 11 seats.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas has rebuked the U.S. State Department for its remarks about the Indonesian general election, calling them "inappropriate". State Department Spokesman John Dinger has described the Indonesian electoral system as being so tightly controlled by the government and that it severely limited political competition.
Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo has hinted that government offices and state firms would soon have to buy Timor car sedans to prop up the national car's slumping sales.
A revote will be held in Sampang on Madura island after an angry crowd burned ballot boxes on election day last Thursday, alleging election rigging.
